data.command: How does persistence via scheduled tasks work?

data.text:
Scheduled-task persistence works by registering an action with a service that re-executes it on a timer, so it survives reboots and needs no interactive session. The main facilities on this host:

cron — per-user crontabs in /var/spool/cron/crontabs/<user> (edited with crontab -e), system jobs in /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.d/, and the packaged /etc/cron.{hourly,daily,weekly,monthly} drop-ins. A job runs as the user that owns the crontab, at the schedule in the five time fields.

anacron — catches up missed daily/weekly/monthly jobs on machines that are not always up; driven by the anacron and cron. timer units.

systemd timers — a .timer unit plus its matching .service unit, enabled with systemctl enable --now <name>.timer; user-level variants live in ~/.config/systemd/user and need lingering. The timers own /lib/systemd/system and /etc/systemd/system.

at — one-shot delayed jobs read by atd from /var/spool/at.

Writability is the whole game: any location this account (or root) can write becomes a persistence point. Detecting it means walking all of those locations rather than trusting crontab -l alone.

webapp@web-srv-01:~$ crontab -l
# m  h  dom mon dow   command
/5     /usr/bin/php /var/www/app/artisan schedule:run >> /var/log/webapp-scheduler.log 2>&1
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ ls -la /etc/cron.d/ /etc/cron.hourly/ /etc/cron.daily/

webapp@web-srv-01:~$ cat /etc/crontab
# /etc/crontab: system-wide crontab
SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin
HOME=/root
LOGNAME=root

17 	  	root    cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.hourly
25 6	  	root	test -x /usr/sbin/anacron || ( cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.daily )
47 6	  7	root	test -x /usr/sbin/anacron || ( cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.weekly )
52 6	1  	root	test -x /usr/sbin/anacron || ( cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.monthly )
